description:
DANCING WITH THE SARS. 
Basée principalement à RDC, principalement dans la ville Kolwezi (Capitale mondiale du Cobalt), notre équipe se veut faire une analyse des changements des surfaces AU CENTIMÈTRES PRÈS. 
À travers une expertise de Géologue, Environnementaliste, Cartographe-SIG et ingénieur minier, l'équipe tient ses atouts pour aborder un thème bien fascinant dans cet extase.
summary:
Mining around Kolwezi, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, is reshaping 
the land quickly and creating risks for communities and ecosystems. Field surveys 
are slow and costly, and optical satellite images are often blocked by clouds. 
Lualaba SARdance uses free Sentinel-1 radar images (2017–2025), processed in 
Google Earth Engine and mapped in QGIS, to follow how the mining footprint 
changes in the Kamoto mining zone particularly and in the Lualaba province 
generally.
Visual comparison of the yearly radar composites shows a progressive expansion 
of mining surfaces, mainly in the center and south-west of the zone, at the expense 
of the surrounding vegetation. The approach is cloud-independent, low-cost and 
repeatable at other sites. It detects surface change; it does not yet measure ground 
deformation, and it has not yet been validated in the field.
details: The project answers the challenge by applying a SAR time-series analysis to surface change around an active mining area. In this frrst version we used Sentinel=! (ESA) because it offers a long free archive, which allows us to look back to 20/7. We did not use NASA datasets in this version. NASA-ISRO's NISAR mission made its L-band radar data public in July 2026, for observations acquired from 17 June 2026. NISAR and NASA's OPERA products have not yet been integrated and are the first priority for the next version.
